name: Papua New Guinea
headline: Papua New Guinea has moved from forecast risk to observed impact: water sources are drying, crops are failing and food prices are rising ahead of the agricultural peak expected from November 2026, and some 1.2 million people are estimated to require direct food relief (UN PNG, 1 Oct 2026). Highland frost has destroyed gardens for almost four months in Goilala District, and 65.8 per cent of 114 assessed health facilities need urgent attention. The Government declared the event in June, approved a US$112 million supplementary budget and began releasing K2.5 million per district from 21 September, but no pre-arranged CERF or FAO–WFP anticipatory financing is in place for PNG.

hazard_outlook.text: ACCESS-S shows below-normal rainfall over most of PNG (PNG-NWS, 24 Jul 2026); PNG is among the locations with the highest chance of very dry conditions, below 25% of normal rainfall (Earth Sciences NZ, ICU #310, Aug 2026).

Very high climate concern, drier (FAO/WFP/UN Women/WMO/OCHA, 28 Aug 2026); Earth Sciences NZ gives a large dry arc from western Micronesia and PNG with many locations at high chance of extremely dry conditions (Waatea News, 6 Sep 2026).

ECMWF SEAS5, analysed by OCHA's Centre for Humanitarian Data, projects the lowest Oct–Dec rainfall on record (since 1981) for PNG (CERF secretariat, 30 Jun 2026); UN PNG expects the peak around October–December, with agricultural impacts from November (UN PNG, 1 Oct 2026).
A below-average December–March rainy season is expected, so the wet season is not forecast to relieve the deficit (ACAPS, 7 Jul 2026).

Conditions may persist into March–May 2027, with recovery planning in 2027 (UN PNG, 1 Oct 2026); Earth Sciences NZ does not expect a return to ENSO-neutral before April–May 2027 (PACNEWS, 10 Sep 2026).

timeline.label: Apr 2026
timeline.event: Tropical Cyclone Maila affected 143,259 people in PNG, including 81,944 children, and displaced 15,723; at least 41 health facilities were damaged.

timeline.label: Jun 2026
timeline.event: Frost struck the PNG highlands, the first frost event of the June–August window.

timeline.label: Jun 2026
timeline.event: The Government declared the El Niño event; the Prime Minister asked provinces and districts to map water sources, vulnerable communities and food risks.
timeline.source: UN News (citing UN PNG Snapshot); ABC News

timeline.label: 24 Jul 2026
timeline.event: PNG-NWS placed the National Capital District at drought critical and 14 provinces at drought alert; seven provinces escalated from watch to alert in one month.

timeline.label: 31 Jul 2026
timeline.event: Drought and frost damaged food gardens in more than 12 villages in Goilala District, Central Province, affecting over 1,000 people; low Sepik River levels disrupted transport and medical supply delivery.

timeline.label: Aug 2026
timeline.event: An assessment of 114 health facilities found 65.8% needing urgent attention and 55.3% reporting disrupted maternity services.

timeline.label: 16 Sep 2026
timeline.event: Frost had destroyed gardens in Kosipe, Goilala District, for almost four months; low water halted Fly River trade and Lake Murray was drying; the Government allocated an additional K500 million.

timeline.label: 21 Sep 2026
timeline.event: The Prime Minister ordered release of K2.5 million to every district and each provincial government and K5 million to the National Disaster Centre.

timeline.label: 1 Oct 2026
timeline.event: UN PNG estimated some 1.2 million people require direct food relief, with the drought signal spreading from the Highlands to lowland and island provinces.

timeline.label: 19 Oct 2026
timeline.event: SPC reported drought and frost damage in parts of PNG and declining commercial purse-seine tuna catches.

points: Some 1.2 million people are estimated to require direct food relief, with dwindling food reserves and food prices rising months before the worst agricultural impacts expected from November 2026 (UN News, 7 Oct 2026, citing UN PNG Snapshot of 1 Oct 2026).

Crops planted in June are unlikely to produce a harvest and earlier plantings may yield less than half, in some cases a quarter, of expectations; shortages remain highly localised but are feared to become widespread (ABC News, 16 Sep 2026).

Drought and frost damaged food gardens in more than 12 villages in Goilala District, affecting over 1,000 people; Chimbu, Western Highlands, Oro and Eastern Highlands reported crop failures and bushfires (PNG DMT, 31 Jul 2026).
PNG-NWS assesses that in the National Capital District basic water and electricity services are likely to be affected (PNG-NWS, 24 Jul 2026).
Port Moresby's ageing water infrastructure was at risk of failure, threatening services for 756,754 residents, including 325,404 children (UNICEF EAPRO, 30 Jun 2026).
Lake Murray was drying, leaving thousands in Middle Fly District short of water (ABC News, 16 Sep 2026).

Of 114 health facilities assessed in August 2026, 65.8% need urgent attention, ~79% report water sources drying, 55.3% report disrupted maternity services and 45.6% report a moderate rise in malnutrition (UN PNG, 1 Oct 2026).
A vaccine-derived poliovirus outbreak continues; the June 2026 national campaign round vaccinated 333,392 children (UNICEF EAPRO, 30 Jun 2026).
Smoke from Indonesian forest fires was crossing into PNG by early September (PACNEWS/Insurance Business, 10 Sep 2026).
The Education Department established an El Niño taskforce to address potential impacts on schools (PNG DMT, 31 Jul 2026).
In Kosipe, Goilala District, schoolteachers left classrooms to forage for food, leaving schoolchildren without lessons (ABC News, 16 Sep 2026).
Low Sepik River levels disrupted river transport, market access and delivery of medical supplies in East Sepik (PNG DMT, 31 Jul 2026).
Low water halted river trade on the Fly River route in Western Province, pushing essential goods onto roads (ABC News, 16 Sep 2026).
Commercial purse-seine catches are declining, reducing earnings from fishing licences and commercial fishing (PINA/SPC, 19 Oct 2026).
PNG has a high pre-existing GBV risk level; Highlands drought is assessed as driving intimate partner violence through livelihood collapse (GBV Coordination Asia Pacific / REGA, Q2 2026).

The GBV Sub-Sector is the only active protection coordination mechanism, as the Protection Sector is inactive in PNG, and it is overburdened and under-resourced (GBV Coordination Asia Pacific / REGA, Q2 2026).
The Police Minister instructed police to act where food and water pressure could inflame inter-community tensions (ABC News, 16 Sep 2026).
Unsubsidised petrol rose ~36% and diesel ~67% in April, offset by a K1 billion fuel-relief package (FAO/WFP/UN Women/WMO/OCHA, 28 Aug 2026).

ADB marked down PNG's growth forecast in September, citing a more intense El Niño and weaker mining output, after holding it at 3.6% for 2026 in July; PNG inflation may accelerate on El Niño-driven food prices (ADB ADO, 23 Sep 2026).

The Government declared the event in June and runs a whole-of-government response through the ENSO Task Force under the National Disaster Centre, with the NEOC and provincial EOCs activated and a US$112 million supplementary budget (UN PNG, 1 Oct 2026).

An additional K500 million was allocated; from 21 September K2.5 million was released to every district and each provincial government and K5 million to the National Disaster Centre, with a further K2.5 million per district to follow on reporting (ABC News, 16 Sep 2026; The PNG Sun, 21 Sep 2026).

The Food Security Cluster's El Niño Plan of Action for Agricultural Drought (August 2026), led by the Department of Agriculture and Livestock and FAO, phases preparedness, anticipatory action, response and recovery under the 2026–2027 National ENSO Response and Relief Program (FAO/WFP/UN Women/WMO/OCHA, 28 Aug 2026).

A One UN inter-agency response spans food security, nutrition, WASH, health, shelter/CCCM, protection, education, logistics and RCCE, with GBV risk mitigation integrated and supplies prepositioned (UN PNG, 1 Oct 2026).

Following UNICEF-supported anticipatory assessment, the NCD Provincial Health Authority installed four 9,000-litre water tanks in three clinics, supporting about 770 outpatient consultations per day (UNICEF EAPRO, 30 Jun 2026).
UNICEF pre-positioned 150 dignity kits and 150 WASH hygiene kits in Western Highlands and signed a contingency agreement with ADRA PNG for El Niño education response (UNICEF EAPRO, 30 Jun 2026).
PNG runs FAO's Combined Drought Index as an operational anticipatory-action trigger, one of two countries in Asia-Pacific to do so (FAO/OCHA/WMO/WFP, 17 Jun 2026).

PNG holds no CERF anticipatory-action framework and is not among the four Asia-Pacific priority countries of the FAO–WFP US$202 million anticipatory-action appeal; CERF's Pacific action window is prepositioning before November 2026 (CERF secretariat, 30 Jun 2026).
The El Niño Early Action Plan dates from 2017, and no update or activation for 2026–27 is reported (FAO/OCHA/WMO/WFP, 17 Jun 2026).

history: 1997–98: combined drought and frost cut crop yields by up to 80 per cent in many areas (OCHA ROAP, 20 May 2026); 1.2 million people required food assistance, about a third of the affected population, and relief arrived after food stocks were exhausted (UN PNG, 1 Oct 2026).

2015–16: from April 2015, drought and repeated frosts at 2,200–2,800 m produced severe food insecurity and malnutrition affecting 224,000 people (OCHA ROAP, 20 May 2026); 2.7 million people were affected (WFP, Jun 2026) and 540,000 assisted, with assessment reaching province level only (UN PNG, 1 Oct 2026).
2015–16: PNG received US$4.7 million from CERF for drought; it received nothing in 2023–24 (CERF secretariat, 30 Jun 2026).
2023–24: subsistence farmers in PNG and Vanuatu faced severe food shortages as drought destroyed sweet potato and taro (OCHA ROAP, 20 May 2026).
cautions: The PNG-NWS July bulletin omits Eastern Highlands from its alert table but lists it at alert in its provinces-of-concern text; the wiki follows the text. Oro, at watch only, was among provinces reporting impacts (PNG-NWS, 24 Jul 2026; PNG DMT, 31 Jul 2026).
The 1.2 million figure is a targeting assumption (20% of 3.89 million people in alert census units plus 20% of 1.94 million in critical units), not a count (UN PNG, 1 Oct 2026).

Historical caseloads differ: 2.7 million affected in 2015–16 (WFP; UN PNG), an estimated 3 million affected in a past powerful event, year unstated (Oxfam), and 224,000 in severe food insecurity and malnutrition (OCHA ROAP); the 1997–98 'a third of the affected' implies roughly 3.6 million affected (derived). No source states the relationship.
Rankings diverge: PNG is Tier 1 in the 28 Aug regional snapshot but only in the monitoring tier of the IASC ENSO Cell, which weights existing caseloads and fragility.
ABC gives the K500 million allocation as "$157 million" without stating the currency (ABC News, 16 Sep 2026).
